# buttons.article

Build a native inline article whose selected result sends literal text.

## Signature

```python
def buttons.article(id: str, title: str, text: str, *, description: str | None = None, reply_markup: Any | None = None, entities: list[Any] | None = None) -> InputBotInlineResult
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Python type | Default | Passing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str` | `Required` | Positional or keyword |
| `title` | `str` | `Required` | Positional or keyword |
| `text` | `str` | `Required` | Positional or keyword |
| `description` | `str \| None` | `None` | Keyword-only |
| `reply_markup` | `Any \| None` | `None` | Keyword-only |
| `entities` | `list[Any] \| None` | `None` | Keyword-only |

### id

Inline result identifier string containing 1–64 UTF-8 bytes. Distinct results in one answer must have unique IDs. It is not a message ID.

### title

Visible article-result title. The sent text comes from the separate text argument.

### text

Literal text that will be sent when the article is chosen. It is not a description label; supply explicit native MessageEntity objects for formatting.

### description

Description text. For set_chat_description this is the chat's about field, and empty text clears it. For inline article results it is optional listing text, not the sent message body.

**Omission:** the Python default is None. It is not automatically equivalent to an empty string, zero, False or an empty collection. The behavior above defines this method's interpretation.

### reply_markup

Native ReplyMarkup object, usually buttons.inline([...]) for an inline keyboard. None omits markup in the request. Editing omission is not a guaranteed instruction to remove existing markup; use an explicit supported raw operation when removal semantics matter.

**Omission:** the Python default is None. It is not automatically equivalent to an empty string, zero, False or an empty collection. The behavior above defines this method's interpretation.

### entities

Explicit native MessageEntity objects. Entity offsets and lengths use Telegram UTF-16 code units, not Python string indices for non-BMP characters. None omits the optional field; an empty list explicitly supplies no entities.

**Omission:** the Python default is None. It is not automatically equivalent to an empty string, zero, False or an empty collection. The behavior above defines this method's interpretation.

## Returns

types.InputBotInlineResult with InputBotInlineMessageText.

## Example

```python
from gramflux import Client, Session, buttons, filters
from gramflux.raw import types

article = buttons.article("intro", "Introduction", "Hello", description="Read the introduction")
await client.answer_inline_query(event.query_id, [article])
```

## Constraints and failure behavior

A result ID must be 1–64 UTF-8 bytes. Title/listing description and sent text are separate. Telegram enforces account, result and formatting rules.

These examples assume a previously constructed client where one is used. Builders and selectors do not make a network request by themselves. Invalid builder/selector inputs raise ConfigurationError or the underlying Python argument/regex error. Session I/O errors arise when storage is actually opened during connect.
